title: Equivariant Borsuk-Ulam: Extensions to Other Group Actions

problemStatement.formal: \text{For a finite group } G \text{ acting freely on } S^n, \text{ characterize when a } G\text{-equivariant continuous } f: S^n \to S^k \text{ must vanish or what dimension bound on } k \text{ applies.}
problemStatement.plain: The classical Borsuk-Ulam theorem (Z/2 action: x ↦ -x) has equivariant generalizations to other group actions. For Z/p (prime p), Yang-Borsuk (1954) proves that equivariant maps must vanish. Dold's theorem (1983) gives a cohomological obstruction for general finite groups. The open questions concern non-prime groups, non-free actions, and compact Lie groups.
whyMatters: Connects group theory (G-actions), topology (sphere maps), and algebra (equivariant maps)
The Z/p case is settled via Yang-Borsuk; composite order groups are more subtle
Dold's theorem provides the general framework but is not computable
Applications in combinatorics: topological lower bounds for chromatic numbers

insights: Z/2 equivariance = odd function: f(-x) = -f(x) iff Z/2-equivariant; classical BU proved via difference function g(x)=f(x)-f(-x) which is odd
Key: g(x) = f(x)-f(-x) vanishes at some sphere point by BU → f(x) = f(-x) there
Z/p rotation action on R^2: rotate by 2π/p, isometry by cos²+sin²=1 (sorry needed for EuclideanSpace.equiv formalism)
Yang-Borsuk (1954): for prime p, Z/p free action on S^(2n-1), equivariant maps to S^(2n-3) vanish — proved via p-th roots of unity Z/p-equivariant covering
Dold's theorem (1983): If G acts freely on (n-1)-connected space X and dim Y < n, then no G-equivariant map X → Y. Proof: cohomological index / Borel construction
Fadell-Husseini ideal-valued cohomological index (1988): systematic approach; not in Mathlib
For composite order: use Sylow subgroups — Z/p^k subgroup of Z/6 (p=2 or 3) gives Yang-Borsuk type result
The Z/p freeness on S^(2n-1): ω^k·z=z with z≠0 requires ω^k=1 in each complex coordinate, but ω=e^(2πi/p) is a primitive root, so k≡0 (mod p)
